mainTopic: Who is exempt from ראייה, and the חכמים who cried at פסוקים about closeness to ה׳ and Divine judgment
overview: The amud opens by finishing a point about the מפונק, a pampered person who cannot walk barefoot and so is exempt from ראייה, proven from ישעיהו. A ברייתא then says the ערל and the טמא are exempt too. The גמרא finds the טמא's source in the link between 'coming' and 'bringing.' It explains the ערל by saying the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who treats a ערל like a טמא. Another ברייתא repeats the טמא's exemption and adds that a person blind in one eye is exempt, learned from reading the פסוק as both 'will see' and 'will be seen.' From there the גמרא turns to מוסר: רב הונא, רבי אלעזר, רבי אמי, רבי אסי and רב יוסף each cried at certain פסוקים, out of fear of being pushed away, fear of Divine judgment, and the uncertainty of 'perhaps.' רב יוסף's question, whether someone can die before his time, is answered with the story of the מלאך המוות's messenger who took the wrong מרים. That story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The delicate person is exempt, proven from ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: the extra wording comes to include the מפונק, a pampered person who cannot walk barefoot, and proves it from ישעיהו 1:12.
steps.simpleTranslation: The extra words come to include delicate people, as it says: 'When you come to appear before Me, who asked this of you, to trample My courts?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer that began before this section. It says a pampered person who cannot go barefoot is also exempt from ראייה, and brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא calls coming into the בית המקדש with shoes 'trampling My courts.' Someone who cannot walk barefoot would have to come that way. So he is not included in the מצוה of ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: Delicate, pampered people who cannot walk barefoot
The מצוה of appearing in the בית המקדש on the רגלים

steps.whatToRemember: A מפונק, who cannot enter the בית המקדש barefoot, is exempt from ראייה.

phrases.english: Delicate people, as it is written:
phrases.notes: People too pampered to walk without shoes.

phrases.english: "When you come to appear before Me,
who asked this of your hand,
to trample My courts?"

steps.triggerLanguage: מְפַנְּקִי, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from before this section about whom the extra wording includes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra wording includes the מפונק, who is exempt because coming in with shoes is called 'trampling My courts.'

steps.title: A ברייתא: the uncircumcised and the impure are exempt
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a ערל and a טמא are both exempt from ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: An uncircumcised man and an impure person are exempt from appearing in the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that adds two more people who are exempt from ראייה: the ערל and the טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new source with a plain ruling. It does not give reasons. The next steps will look for the source of each exemption.

phrases.english: It was taught: The uncircumcised and the impure
are exempt from appearing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הֶעָרֵל וְהַטָּמֵא פְּטוּרִין מִן הָרְאִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more people to the list of those exempt from ראייה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ערל and a טמא are exempt from ראייה.

steps.title: The impure person's exemption comes from 'coming' and 'bringing'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the טמא's exemption is understood: two nearby פסוקים link 'coming' to the בית המקדש with 'bringing' קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, an impure person is exempt, since it says 'And there you shall come' and 'And there you shall bring.' Whoever is included in coming is included in bringing, and whoever is not included in coming is not included in bringing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the easy half of the ברייתא, the טמא. This is the first half of a 'granted... but' pattern, so it sets up the question coming next about the ערל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים put 'coming' (ביאה) right next to 'bringing' (הבאה). A טמא may not enter the בית המקדש, so he is not part of 'coming.' Because of the link, he is also not obligated to bring the עולת ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part is understood (sets up a 'but' question)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse ביאה (coming) with הבאה (bringing). The words look alike, but the whole proof depends on tying the two together.

phrases.english: Granted, an impure person —
as it is written: "And there you shall come"
"and there you shall bring,"
whoever is included in coming —
is included in bringing,
and whoever is not included in coming —
is not included in bringing.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא טָמֵא — דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the טמא half of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The nearby פסוקים 'ובאת שמה' and 'והבאתם שמה' (דברים 12:5-6), which link coming with bringing

steps.title: Where do we learn the uncircumcised man's exemption?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a ערל is exempt from ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But an uncircumcised man, from where do we know he is exempt?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the 'granted... but' pattern. The טמא is clear, but nothing so far shows that a ערל is barred from the בית המקדש or exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'coming and bringing' proof only works for someone who may not enter. A ערל is not obviously in that group, so the ברייתא's ruling about him needs a source.

phrases.english: But the uncircumcised, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עָרֵל מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the easy case (טמא) to the hard case (ערל).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a ערל is exempt from ראייה.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who treats a ערל like a טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who puts the ערל in the same category as the טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? It is רבי עקיבא's, who includes the uncircumcised man like the impure person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by naming the author of the ברייתא: רבי עקיבא. In his view a ערל has the same status as a טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a ערל is treated like a טמא, the 'coming and bringing' rule from step 3 covers him too. So no separate source for ראייה is needed, only proof that רבי עקיבא holds this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Includes (from an extra word in the פסוק)

phrases.english: Whose is this?
It is רבי עקיבא,
who includes the uncircumcised like the impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the ערל by naming the ברייתא's author.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who treats a ערל like a טמא, so the same exemption applies.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the ערל from the double word 'איש איש'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא showing that רבי עקיבא learns from the doubled 'איש איש' that a ערל is included with the טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי עקיבא says, 'A man, a man' comes to include the uncircumcised.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its claim about רבי עקיבא by quoting his words in another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'איש איש' instead of just 'איש.' רבי עקיבא reads the extra word as adding the ערל to the rules of the טמא. This confirms the answer in step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A man, a man,' a doubled word in the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא, a ערל is like a טמא, so both are exempt from ראייה.

phrases.english: As it was taught: רבי עקיבא says:
"A man, a man"
comes to include the uncircumcised.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves that רבי עקיבא holds the view given in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי עקיבא's view that a ערל is treated like a טמא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי עקיבא reads 'איש איש' (ויקרא 22:4) as including the ערל

steps.title: A new ברייתא repeats the impure person's exemption
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of the תנו רבנן type teaches that a טמא is exempt from ראייה, using the same 'coming and bringing' proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: An impure person is exempt from appearing, since it says 'And there you shall come' and 'And there you shall bring.' Whoever is included in coming is included in bringing, and whoever is not included in coming is not included in bringing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new ברייתא that says outright what step 3 explained: a טמא is exempt from ראייה. The same ברייתא goes on in the next step to add the person blind in one eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 was the גמרא's own explanation. Here a ברייתא states the same proof as a teaching of the תנאים. The wording is repeated because the גמרא quotes this ברייתא in full, and its next clause, the one-eyed person in step 8, is the new teaching.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
An impure person is exempt from appearing,
as it is written: "And there you shall come"
"and there you shall bring."
Whoever is included in coming —
is included in bringing,
and whoever is not included in coming —
is not included in bringing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: טָמֵא פָּטוּר מִן הָרְאִיָּיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that states the same proof the גמרא used in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טמא is exempt from ראייה, because whoever cannot 'come' to the בית המקדש is not obligated in 'bringing.'

steps.title: A person blind in one eye is exempt from ראייה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי, quoting רבי יהודה, rules that a person blind in one eye is exempt from ראייה. He learns it from reading the word in the פסוק two ways: יִרְאֶה (he will see) and יֵרָאֶה (he will be seen).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן דהבאי says in the name of רבי יהודה: a person blind in one eye is exempt from ראייה. The פסוק can be read 'he will see' and also 'he will be seen'. This teaches that he comes to be seen the same way he comes to see. Just as he sees with both eyes, he must also come to be seen with both eyes.
steps.whatsHappening: The list of people exempt from ראייה continues. Now a new person is added: someone blind in one eye.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The written word can be read יִרְאֶה (he will see) or יֵרָאֶה (he will be seen). רבי יהודה joins the two readings. Being seen in the בית המקדש is modeled on seeing, and seeing means with both eyes. So someone with only one working eye does not fit the מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He will see' / 'he will be seen'. These are two ways to read the same written word.
In the same way that... so too...

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about someone fully blind. Even a person who sees perfectly with one eye is exempt, because the rule needs 'both eyes'.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Dehavai says in the name of Rabbi Yehudah:

phrases.aramaic: סוֹמֵא בְּאַחַת מֵעֵינָיו פָּטוּר מִן הָרְאִיָּיה,
phrases.english: One who is blind in one of his eyes is exempt from the מצוה of appearing,
as it says: 'he will see' / 'he will be seen',
phrases.notes: שמות 23:17. The same letters can be read both ways, and רבי יהודה uses both readings.

phrases.english: in the same way that he comes to see,
so he comes to be seen.
Just as he comes to see with both his eyes,
so too, he comes to be seen with both his eyes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן דַּהֲבַאי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא from step 7, adding another person exempt from ראייה: one who is blind in one eye.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person blind in one eye is exempt from ראייה, because seeing and being seen must both be with two eyes.

steps.title: רב הונא cries over 'seeing and being seen'
steps.stepSummary: When רב הונא reached the פסוק that reads 'will see / will be seen', he cried. He feared that a servant whose Master longs to see him could end up pushed away, as ישעיהו says.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא reached this פסוק, 'he will see / he will be seen', he cried. He said: a servant whose master waits eagerly to see him, and he will be pushed away from him? As it is written: 'When you come to appear before Me, who asked this of you, to trample My courtyards?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from הלכה to a story. רב הונא cried when he learned the ראייה פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double reading shows how close the relationship is: הקדוש ברוך הוא wants to see us just as we come to see Him. Yet the פסוק in ישעיהו shows that the same visits can become unwanted 'trampling' when people sin. Losing such closeness is what made רב הונא cry.

keyTerms.meaning: Will be pushed away / kept at a distance

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the גמרא's legal reading of יִרְאֶה / יֵרָאֶה also carries a deep emotional meaning about our closeness to הקדוש ברוך הוא.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא
phrases.english: When Rav Huna reached this verse,
'he will see' / 'he will be seen', he cried.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: עֶבֶד שֶׁרַבּוֹ מְצַפֶּה לוֹ לִרְאוֹתוֹ
phrases.english: He said: a servant whose master eagerly waits to see him,
will he be pushed away from him?
As it is written: 'When you come to appear before Me,'

phrases.aramaic: מִי בִקֵּשׁ זֹאת מִיֶּדְכֶם רְמוֹס חֲצֵרָי״.
phrases.english: 'who asked this of you, to trample My courtyards?'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the double reading יִרְאֶה / יֵרָאֶה from step 8 and gives it an emotional, non-legal meaning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The servant whom the Master longs to see can, through sin, become a visitor who is not wanted.

steps.title: רב הונא cries over eating at the Master's table
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא also cried at the פסוק about eating שלמים 'there', meaning before ה׳. A servant invited to his Master's table could still be rejected, as ישעיהו says.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא reached this פסוק, he cried: 'You shall offer שלמים and eat there.' A servant whose master expects him to eat at his table, will he be pushed away from him? As it is written: 'What do I need your many offerings for? says ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second story of רב הונא crying. This one follows the same pattern as the first, but with eating instead of seeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating שלמים in the בית המקדש is like being a guest at the King's table, which is a sign of closeness. But ישעיהו shows that ה׳ can say He doesn't want the offerings. The same fear returns: the invited servant could be pushed away.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offerings, whose meat the owners eat

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי:
phrases.english: When Rav Huna reached this verse, he cried:
'And you shall offer peace-offerings and eat there.'

phrases.aramaic: עֶבֶד שֶׁרַבּוֹ מְצַפֶּה לֶאֱכוֹל עַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ
phrases.english: A servant whose master expects him to eat at his table,
will he be pushed away from him?

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְתִיב: ״לָמָּה לִּי רוֹב זִבְחֵיכֶם יֹאמַר ה׳״.
phrases.english: As it is written: 'What do I need your many offerings for? says the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel to step 9 that uses the same 'servant pushed away' pattern, this time for eating instead of seeing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even the servant invited to his Master's table can be rejected if his offerings are unwanted.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר cries over the brothers' silence before יוסף
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר cried at the פסוק saying יוסף's brothers could not answer him. If a human's rebuke left them speechless, how much more will the rebuke of הקדוש ברוך הוא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אלעזר reached this פסוק, he cried: 'And his brothers could not answer him, because they were terrified before him.' If the rebuke of a human being is like this, the rebuke of הקדוש ברוך הוא is all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the stories of חכמים crying. Now רבי אלעזר uses a קל וחומר from יוסף and his brothers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף only said 'I am יוסף', and his brothers were left with no answer. That was a rebuke from a human being. So the rebuke of הקדוש ברוך הוא on the day of judgment will be far harder to face.

keyTerms.meaning: Flesh and blood, meaning a human being
All the more so (the wording of a קל וחומר)

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Elazar reached this verse, he cried:
'And his brothers could not answer him,'
'because they were terrified before him.'
phrases.notes: בראשית 45:3, right after יוסף tells his brothers who he is.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה תּוֹכֵחָה שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם כָּךְ,
phrases.english: If the rebuke of a human being is like this,

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹכֵחָה שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא — עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה.
phrases.english: the rebuke of the Holy One, Blessed be He, all the more so.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps the series of 'when he reached this פסוק, he cried' going, now with רבי אלעזר and a new theme: fear of Divine rebuke.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קל וחומר: if a human's rebuke left the brothers speechless, Divine rebuke will be much more overwhelming.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר cries over שמואל's fear of judgment
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר cried at שמואל's words to שאול after being brought up from the dead. If שמואל the צדיק feared judgment, we must fear it all the more.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אלעזר reached this פסוק, he cried: 'And שמואל said to שאול: Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?' If שמואל the צדיק was afraid of judgment, how much more so should we be.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר cries a second time and makes another קל וחומר, this time from שמואל. More stories of חכמים crying follow in the coming steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל was disturbed at being brought up, because he was afraid of the judgment. If a great צדיק like שמואל feared the דין, ordinary people should fear it even more. Step 13 asks what shows that שמואל was afraid.

keyTerms.meaning: You disturbed me / shook me up
To bring me up (from the dead)

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא has moved from הלכה (who is exempt from ראייה) to מוסר. A series of חכמים cried at certain פסוקים: רב הונא feared being pushed away, and רבי אלעזר feared Divine judgment. More examples follow.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Elazar reached this verse, he cried:
'And Samuel said to Saul:'
'Why have you disturbed me by bringing me up?'
phrases.notes: שמואל א 28:15. שאול had שמואל brought up from the dead.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה שְׁמוּאֵל הַצַּדִּיק הָיָה מִתְיָירֵא מִן הַדִּין,
phrases.english: If Samuel the righteous was afraid of judgment,
we, all the more so!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second crying story from רבי אלעזר, built as another קל וחומר like step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If even שמואל the צדיק feared Divine judgment, ordinary people must fear it all the more.

steps.title: What did שמואל fear?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what shows that שמואל feared judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the story with שמואל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to step 12, where we said שמואל feared judgment, and asks where we see that. It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said שמואל was afraid but did not show it. Here the גמרא asks for the source, so we can see that fear inside the פסוקים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (asking for the details or the source)

phrases.english: Samuel, what is it?
phrases.notes: He means: what shows that שמואל was afraid of being judged, as we said just before?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the background to רבי אלעזר's statement about שמואל in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where we see that שמואל feared judgment.

steps.title: שמואל brought משה along as a witness
steps.stepSummary: The plural word עולים shows that two came up. The second was משה, whom שמואל brought to testify that he kept the whole תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the woman told שאול, 'I see a godlike being coming up (עולים).' The word עולים is plural, so it means two. One was שמואל. The other was משה, because שמואל went and brought משה with him. He said to משה: 'Maybe, Heaven forbid, I am being called to judgment. Stand with me, because there is nothing you wrote in the תורה that I did not keep.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading the פסוק closely. The plural word 'coming up' shows that שמואל did not come alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra figure in the פסוק is explained as משה. שמואל thought he was being raised for judgment and wanted משה, who wrote the תורה, to testify for him. This shows how much even a צדיק like שמואל feared Heaven's judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: I am being summoned to judgment

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And the woman said to Saul,
I see a godlike being coming up [olim].'
'Olim' (coming up) means two:
one is Samuel, and the other —
Samuel went and brought Moses with him.
He said to him: Perhaps, Heaven forbid,
I am being summoned to judgment; stand with me,
for there is nothing that you wrote in the Torah
that I did not fulfill.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַתֹּאמֶר הָאִשָּׁה אֶל שָׁאוּל אֱלֹהִים רָאִיתִי עוֹלִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The plural עולים shows that שמואל brought משה to testify that he kept the whole תורה, because he feared judgment.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the theme of these steps: even the greatest צדיקים were afraid of Heaven's judgment.

steps.title: רבי אמי cries over 'perhaps there may be hope'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי cried because after so much suffering, the פסוק promises only 'perhaps' there is hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אמי reached the פסוק 'Let him put his mouth in the dust, perhaps there may be hope,' he cried. He said: 'All this, and only perhaps?!'
steps.whatsHappening: A new חכם is added to the list of רבנן who cried at certain פסוקים. רבי אמי is pained by the word 'perhaps'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person in the פסוק humbles himself completely, with his mouth in the dust. Even so, hope is only 'perhaps'. That uncertainty is what made רבי אמי cry.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַמֵּי כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Ami reached this verse, he cried:
'Let him put his mouth in the dust,
perhaps there may be hope.'
He said: All this, and only 'perhaps'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of רבנן who cried at פסוקים, the list that began with רב הונא in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even after great humbling, the פסוק promises only possible hope.

steps.title: רבי אמי cries over 'perhaps you will be hidden'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי cried again because seeking righteousness and humility leads only to 'perhaps' being protected on the day of anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אמי reached the פסוק 'Seek righteousness, seek humility; perhaps you will be hidden on the day of ה׳'s anger,' he cried. He said: 'All this, and only perhaps?!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי cries at a second פסוק that has the same 'perhaps'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the effort is active: seeking צדק and humility. Even so, protection is not guaranteed. The pattern is the same as in step 15.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַמֵּי כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Ami reached this verse, he cried:
'Seek righteousness, seek humility;
perhaps you shall be hidden on the day of the Lord's anger.'
He said: All this, and only 'perhaps'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַמֵּי כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second פסוק with the same 'perhaps' pattern.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even seeking righteousness and humility brings only possible protection.

steps.title: רבי אסי cries over 'perhaps ה׳ will be gracious'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי cried because hating evil, loving good and setting up justice lead only to 'perhaps' ה׳ will be gracious.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אסי reached the פסוק 'Hate evil, love good, and set up justice in the gate; perhaps ה׳, the God of hosts, will be gracious,' he cried: 'All this, and only perhaps?!'
steps.whatsHappening: A third פסוק with 'perhaps' is added, this time from רבי אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the list of good deeds is even longer, yet the result is still uncertain. All three פסוקים teach together that no one can feel sure of Heaven's kindness.

keyTerms.meaning: Set up justice in the gate (the courts)

steps.whatToRemember: Three פסוקים end with 'perhaps' even after great effort. That is why the רבנן cried: a person can never take Heaven's favor for granted.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אַסִּי כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי:
phrases.english: When Rabbi Asi reached this verse, he cried:
'Hate the evil, and love the good,
and establish justice in the gate;
perhaps the Lord, the God of hosts, will be gracious.'
phrases.notes: עמוס 5:15. The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: All this, and only 'perhaps'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אַסִּי כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and final 'perhaps' פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a full life of good deeds brings only possible grace.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks: can someone die before his time?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף cried at a פסוק saying some are swept away without justice, and asked whether a person can really die before his time.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יוסף reached the פסוק 'But there are those swept away without justice,' he cried. He said: 'Is there really someone who goes before his time?'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף cries over a new פסוק and raises a question. This sets up the answer and the story that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say that people can die without any judgment against them. רב יוסף asks whether that can truly happen, and the next step answers him.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יוֹסֵף כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי:
phrases.english: When Rav Yosef reached this verse, he cried:
'But there are those swept away without justice.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: מִי אִיכָּא דְּאָזֵיל בְּלָא זִמְנֵיהּ?
phrases.english: He said: Is there one who goes before his time?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יוֹסֵף כִּי מָטֵי לְהַאי קְרָא, בָּכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another חכם who cried at a פסוק, but this time he also asks a question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person can die before his destined time.

steps.title: Yes: the messenger brought the wrong מרים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes, with a story from רב ביבי בר אביי: the מלאך המוות sent his messenger for מרים the hair-braider, but he brought מרים who raised children.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. As in the story of רב ביבי בר אביי, whom the מלאך המוות often visited. The מלאך המוות told his messenger, 'Go bring me מרים the braider of women's hair.' The messenger went and brought מרים who raised small children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב יוסף's question with a yes, and proves it with a story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two women had the same name and similar titles, so the messenger took the wrong one. That second מרים died even though her time had not come.

keyTerms.meaning: One who grows or raises (used for braiding hair and for raising children)

phrases.aramaic: אִין, כִּי הָא דְּרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
phrases.english: Yes, like this story of Rav Beivai bar Abaye:
the Angel of Death was often found with him.
He said to his messenger:
phrases.notes: 'He' here is the מלאך המוות, talking to his helper.

phrases.english: Go bring me Miriam
the braider of women's hair.
phrases.notes: 'Bring me' means take her life. מגדלא literally means 'one who grows', which is the same word used for the other Miriam.

phrases.english: He went, and brought him
Miriam the raiser of small children.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִין, כִּי הָא דְּרַב בִּיבִי בַּר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question in step 18 with a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, a person can die before his time, as happened to the wrong מרים.

steps.title: The mistake is noticed, but she is counted anyway
steps.stepSummary: The מלאך המוות points out the mistake. The messenger offers to bring her back, but he is told to count her among the dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The מלאך המוות said: 'I told you Miriam the braider of women's hair!' The messenger said: 'If so, return her.' He answered: 'Since you already brought her, let her be counted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The mistake is noticed, but it is not undone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the heart of the proof. מרים's death was not decreed, yet she stays among the dead. That is exactly what 'swept away without justice' means.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא מִרְיָם מְגַדְּלָא שֵׂיעָר נְשַׁיָּיא אֲמַרִי לָךְ!
phrases.english: He said to him: I told you Miriam the braider of women's hair!
He said to him: If so, return her!
He said to him: Since you have brought her —
let her be counted in the number!
phrases.notes: He means: count her among the people who have died.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא מִרְיָם מְגַדְּלָא שֵׂיעָר נְשַׁיָּיא אֲמַרִי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wrongly taken מרים stays among the dead, so a person can die before his time.

steps.title: How could her life be taken?
steps.stepSummary: The messenger is asked how he managed to take מרים's life if her time had not come.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how were you able to take her?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question comes up inside the story. It sets up the messenger's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her time had not come, it seems the messenger should not have had power over her. The question asks what gave him the chance.

keyTerms.meaning: How were you able (to overpower) her?

phrases.english: But how were you able to take her?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הֵיכִי יְכֵלְתְּ לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about how the event in steps 19 and 20 could happen.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What gave the messenger power over a woman whose time had not come.

steps.title: She was holding a shovel and lighting a fire
steps.stepSummary: The messenger begins to explain: she was holding a shovel and lighting the oven. The explanation continues after this section.
steps.simpleTranslation: She was holding a shovel in her hand and was lighting...
steps.whatsHappening: The messenger starts to answer, describing what מרים was doing at that moment. The answer finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The details of what she was doing explain how the messenger got his chance. The rest of the explanation comes next on the דף.

phrases.english: She was holding a shovel in her hand
and was lighting

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָת נְקִיטָא מְתָארָא בִּידַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the question in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: What she was doing at that moment gave the messenger his chance; the full explanation continues after this section.
